claim: NOCA-1 is a C. elegans protein with homology to vertebrate ninein.
source: In this study, we identify Caenorhabditis elegans NOCA-1 as a protein with homology to vertebrate ninein.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this identification based on sequence analysis.

claim: NOCA-1 contributes to the assembly of non-centrosomal microtubule arrays in multiple tissues.
source: NOCA-1 contributes to the assembly of non-centrosomal microtubule arrays in multiple tissues.
evidence: The abstract states this as a main finding of the study.

claim: In the larval epidermis, NOCA-1 functions redundantly with Patronin/PTRN-1 to assemble a circumferential microtubule array essential for worm growth and morphogenesis.
source: In the larval epidermis, NOCA-1 functions redundantly with the minus end protection factor Patronin/PTRN-1 to assemble a circumferential microtubule array essential for worm growth and morphogenesis.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes this redundant function based on experimental data.

claim: γ-tubulin acts with NOCA-1 in parallel to Patronin/PTRN-1 in the larval epidermis.
source: Controlled degradation of a γ-tubulin complex subunit in this tissue revealed that γ-tubulin acts with NOCA-1 in parallel to Patronin/PTRN-1.
evidence: The abstract states this finding based on controlled degradation experiments.

claim: NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin co-localize at the cell surface in the germline.
source: In the germline, NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin co-localize at the cell surface, and inhibiting either leads to a microtubule assembly defect.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this co-localization observation.

claim: Inhibiting either NOCA-1 or γ-tubulin leads to a microtubule assembly defect in the germline.
source: In the germline, NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin co-localize at the cell surface, and inhibiting either leads to a microtubule assembly defect.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this phenotypic consequence of inhibition.

claim: γ-tubulin targets independently of NOCA-1 in the germline.
source: γ-tubulin targets independently of NOCA-1, but NOCA-1 targeting requires γ-tubulin when a non-essential putatively palmitoylated cysteine is mutated.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this targeting dependency relationship.

claim: NOCA-1 targeting requires γ-tubulin when a non-essential putatively palmitoylated cysteine is mutated.
source: γ-tubulin targets independently of NOCA-1, but NOCA-1 targeting requires γ-tubulin when a non-essential putatively palmitoylated cysteine is mutated.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conditional dependency based on mutation analysis.

claim: NOCA-1 acts with γ-tubulin to assemble non-centrosomal arrays in multiple tissues.
source: These results show that NOCA-1 acts with γ-tubulin to assemble non-centrosomal arrays in multiple tissues and highlight functional overlap between the ninein and Patronin protein families.
evidence: The abstract concludes this based on the cumulative results.

claim: There is functional overlap between the ninein and Patronin protein families.
source: These results show that NOCA-1 acts with γ-tubulin to assemble non-centrosomal arrays in multiple tissues and highlight functional overlap between the ninein and Patronin protein families.
evidence: The abstract concludes this based on the observed redundancy in the larval epidermis.

claim: The noca-1 locus is 23 kb in size.
source: The noca-1 locus is large (23 kb) and more complex than typical for C. elegans genes, encoding eight alternatively spliced isoforms that share a common 466 amino acid C-terminal domain with a predicted coiled-coil region (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states the locus size, and Figure 1A shows the locus structure.

claim: The noca-1 locus encodes eight alternatively spliced isoforms.
source: The noca-1 locus is large (23 kb) and more complex than typical for C. elegans genes, encoding eight alternatively spliced isoforms that share a common 466 amino acid C-terminal domain with a predicted coiled-coil region (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states the number of isoforms, and Figure 1A illustrates them.

claim: All NOCA-1 isoforms share a common 466 amino acid C-terminal domain with a predicted coiled-coil region.
source: The noca-1 locus is large (23 kb) and more complex than typical for C. elegans genes, encoding eight alternatively spliced isoforms that share a common 466 amino acid C-terminal domain with a predicted coiled-coil region (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly describes this shared domain, and Figure 1A shows the domain structure.

claim: The C-terminal domain common to all NOCA-1 isoforms is homologous to the ninein-specific central region of vertebrate ninein.
source: The domain common to NOCA-1 isoforms is homologous to the ninein-specific central region that is absent in ninein-like protein (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this homology, and the figures show the alignment.

claim: The ninein-specific region resides within a larger domain suggested to be required for the microtubule anchoring function of centrosomal ninein.
source: This ninein-specific region resides within a larger domain suggested to be required for the microtubule anchoring function of centrosomal ninein (Delgehyr et al., 2005).
evidence: The text cites a prior study suggesting this functional requirement.

claim: At least four NOCA-1 isoforms are expressed at detectable levels.
source: Immunoblotting with an antibody against the NHD coiled-coil recognized four major species that were absent or strongly reduced in extracts from noca-1∆ and noca-1(RNAi) worms (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicating that at least four isoforms are expressed at detectable levels.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on Western blot data shown in the figures.

claim: noca-1∆ worms are sterile.
source: Consistent with our prior work (Green et al., 2011), noca-1∆ worms were sterile and exhibited germline phenotypes equivalent to γ-tubulin depletion confirming that NOCA-1 has an essential role in assembly of the germline microtubule array.
evidence: The text explicitly states this phenotype.

claim: noca-1∆ worms exhibit germline phenotypes equivalent to γ-tubulin depletion.
source: Consistent with our prior work (Green et al., 2011), noca-1∆ worms were sterile and exhibited germline phenotypes equivalent to γ-tubulin depletion confirming that NOCA-1 has an essential role in assembly of the germline microtubule array.
evidence: The text explicitly states this phenotypic equivalence.

claim: NOCA-1 has an essential role in assembly of the germline microtubule array.
source: Consistent with our prior work (Green et al., 2011), noca-1∆ worms were sterile and exhibited germline phenotypes equivalent to γ-tubulin depletion confirming that NOCA-1 has an essential role in assembly of the germline microtubule array.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the observed phenotypes.

claim: noca-1∆ adult worms appear morphologically normal aside from germline abnormalities.
source: However, aside from germline abnormalities, noca-1∆ adult worms appeared morphologically normal and did not exhibit motility defects (Figure 1D and Video 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation, supported by images and video.

claim: noca-1∆ adult worms do not exhibit motility defects.
source: However, aside from germline abnormalities, noca-1∆ adult worms appeared morphologically normal and did not exhibit motility defects (Figure 1D and Video 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation, supported by video.

claim: ptrn-1∆ worms appear morphologically normal.
source: Like noca-1∆ worms, ptrn-1∆ worms appeared morphologically normal (Chuang et al., 2014; Marcette et al., 2014; Richardson et al., 2014; Figure 1D and Video 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation, supported by images and citations.

claim: ptrn-1∆ worms are fertile.
source: However, in contrast to noca-1∆ worms, ptrn-1∆ worms were fertile, indicating that PTRN-1 function is not required in the germline.
evidence: The text explicitly states this phenotype.

claim: PTRN-1 function is not required in the germline.
source: However, in contrast to noca-1∆ worms, ptrn-1∆ worms were fertile, indicating that PTRN-1 function is not required in the germline.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the fertility of ptrn-1∆ worms.

claim: noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant worms exhibit severe developmental defects.
source: In striking contrast to the two single mutants, noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms exhibited severe developmental defects.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation.

claim: noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant worms grow slowly.
source: Double mutant worms grew slowly, and ∼60% ruptured and died during the first 3 days of post-embryonic development, largely at L4 and early adult stages (Figure 1D–F and Video 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation, supported by figures and video.

claim: Approximately 60% of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant worms rupture and die during the first 3 days of post-embryonic development.
source: Double mutant worms grew slowly, and ∼60% ruptured and died during the first 3 days of post-embryonic development, largely at L4 and early adult stages (Figure 1D–F and Video 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation, supported by figures.

claim: The 40% of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant worms that survive are small and uncoordinated.
source: The 40% that survived were small and uncoordinated (Small Unc; Figure 1E).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation, supported by a figure.

claim: NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 are redundantly required for larval development and viability.
source: We conclude that NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 are redundantly required for larval development and viability.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the double mutant phenotype.

claim: C. elegans PTRN-1 binds to microtubule minus ends.
source: Employing a kinesin gliding assay to define polarity at physiological ionic strength (100 mM KCl), we observed puncta of GFP::PTRN-1 and GFP::DmPatronin at the leading end of gliding microtubules, indicating binding to minus ends (Figure 1G).
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the kinesin gliding assay shown in the figure.

claim: Both NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 co-sediment with microtubules from C. elegans extracts.
source: Both NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 were detected in the pellet after microtubule sedimentation from C. elegans extracts (Figure 1H), indicating that NOCA-1 possesses either a direct or indirect microtubule-binding activity.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on the co-sedimentation assay shown in the figure.

claim: NOCA-1 possesses either a direct or indirect microtubule-binding activity.
source: Both NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 were detected in the pellet after microtubule sedimentation from C. elegans extracts (Figure 1H), indicating that NOCA-1 possesses either a direct or indirect microtubule-binding activity.
evidence: The text explicitly states this inference based on the co-sedimentation data.

claim: Purified GFP-tagged NOCA-1NHD and NOCA-1LICR+NHD are dimeric in 500 mM salt.
source: Hydrodynamic analysis in 500 mM salt indicated that both NOCA-1 fusions were dimeric, whereas GFP-tagged PTRN-1 and DmPatronin were monomeric (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on hydrodynamic analysis shown in the figure supplement.

claim: GFP-tagged PTRN-1 and DmPatronin are monomeric in 500 mM salt.
source: Hydrodynamic analysis in 500 mM salt indicated that both NOCA-1 fusions were dimeric, whereas GFP-tagged PTRN-1 and DmPatronin were monomeric (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on hydrodynamic analysis shown in the figure supplement.

claim: NOCA-1LICR+NHD and NOCA-1NHD precipitate when the ionic strength is lowered to physiological levels.
source: Unfortunately, lowering the ionic strength to physiological levels caused both NOCA-1LICR+NHD and NOCA-1NHD to precipitate.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation.

claim: Small aggregates of GFP::NOCA-1NHD or GFP::NOCA-1LICR+NHD anchor microtubules by binding to their ends.
source: When small aggregates of GFP::NOCA-1NHD or GFP::NOCA-1LICR+NHD were analyzed in a coverslip-anchorage assay, analogous to that performed previously for Patronin (Goodwin and Vale, 2010; Figure 1—figure supplement 5A), they anchored microtubules by binding to their ends (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on the anchorage assay shown in the figure supplement.

claim: MBP::NOCA-1NHD::GFP forms small aggregates that bind along the lengths of microtubules in classical microtubule assay buffer.
source: Similarly, dilution of MBP::NOCA-1NHD::GFP into a classical microtubule assay buffer caused it to form small aggregates that bound along the lengths of microtubules (Figure 1—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on the assay shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Mitotic spindle assembly in the early embryo is not affected by single or double inhibitions of NOCA-1 and PTRN-1.
source: Mitotic spindle assembly in the early embryo and embryonic viability were not affected by either single or double inhibitions of NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that their redundant function essential for larval development is likely in a differentiated tissue, and not in the formation of centrosomal microtubule arrays required for cell division.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Embryonic viability is not affected by single or double inhibitions of NOCA-1 and PTRN-1.
source: Mitotic spindle assembly in the early embryo and embryonic viability were not affected by either single or double inhibitions of NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that their redundant function essential for larval development is likely in a differentiated tissue, and not in the formation of centrosomal microtubule arrays required for cell division.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The redundant function of NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 essential for larval development is likely in a differentiated tissue.
source: Mitotic spindle assembly in the early embryo and embryonic viability were not affected by either single or double inhibitions of NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that their redundant function essential for larval development is likely in a differentiated tissue, and not in the formation of centrosomal microtubule arrays required for cell division.
evidence: The text explicitly states this inference based on the lack of effect on early embryonic processes.

claim: PTRN-1::GFP expressed from its endogenous promoter rescues the synthetic lethality of the noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant.
source: PTRN-1::GFP expressed from its endogenous promoter (Pptrn-1) rescued the synthetic lethality of the noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant (Figure 2A) and localized in multiple tissues, including the larval/adult epidermis, neurons, intestine, and pharynx (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this rescue result based on data shown in the figures.

claim: PTRN-1::GFP expressed from its endogenous promoter localizes in multiple tissues, including the larval/adult epidermis, neurons, intestine, and pharynx.
source: PTRN-1::GFP expressed from its endogenous promoter (Pptrn-1) rescued the synthetic lethality of the noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant (Figure 2A) and localized in multiple tissues, including the larval/adult epidermis, neurons, intestine, and pharynx (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this localization pattern based on imaging shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Selective expression of PTRN-1::GFP in the larval/adult epidermis rescues the lethality and morphology/movement phenotypes of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutants.
source: Selective expression of PTRN-1::GFP in the larval/adult epidermis (Pdpy-7) rescued the lethality and morphology/movement phenotypes of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutants, whereas no rescue was observed following expression in neurons (Prgef-1) or the pharynx and intestine (Ppha-4) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this tissue-specific rescue result based on data shown in the figures.

claim: Expression of PTRN-1::GFP in neurons does not rescue noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutants.
source: Selective expression of PTRN-1::GFP in the larval/adult epidermis (Pdpy-7) rescued the lethality and morphology/movement phenotypes of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutants, whereas no rescue was observed following expression in neurons (Prgef-1) or the pharynx and intestine (Ppha-4) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this lack of rescue based on data shown in the figures.

claim: Expression of PTRN-1::GFP in the pharynx and intestine does not rescue noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutants.
source: Selective expression of PTRN-1::GFP in the larval/adult epidermis (Pdpy-7) rescued the lethality and morphology/movement phenotypes of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutants, whereas no rescue was observed following expression in neurons (Prgef-1) or the pharynx and intestine (Ppha-4) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this lack of rescue based on data shown in the figures.

claim: A transgene encoding NOCA-1d and e isoforms rescues larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms.
source: Transgenes encoding the NOCA-1d and e isoforms or only the d isoform expressed from their endogenous promoters rescued larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms, whereas transgenes encoding the abcfgh (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) or e isoforms did not.
evidence: The text explicitly states this rescue result based on data shown in the figures.

claim: A transgene encoding only the NOCA-1d isoform rescues larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms.
source: Transgenes encoding the NOCA-1d and e isoforms or only the d isoform expressed from their endogenous promoters rescued larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms, whereas transgenes encoding the abcfgh (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) or e isoforms did not.
evidence: The text explicitly states this rescue result based on data shown in the figures.

claim: A transgene encoding NOCA-1 abcfgh isoforms does not rescue larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms.
source: Transgenes encoding the NOCA-1d and e isoforms or only the d isoform expressed from their endogenous promoters rescued larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms, whereas transgenes encoding the abcfgh (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) or e isoforms did not.
evidence: The text explicitly states this lack of rescue based on data shown in the figures.

claim: A transgene encoding only the NOCA-1e isoform does not rescue larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms.
source: Transgenes encoding the NOCA-1d and e isoforms or only the d isoform expressed from their endogenous promoters rescued larval development in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ worms, whereas transgenes encoding the abcfgh (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) or e isoforms did not.
evidence: The text explicitly states this lack of rescue based on data shown in the figures.

claim: The short NOCA-1d isoform consists of the NHD and a short unique N-terminal extension.
source: The short NOCA-1d isoform consists of the NHD and a short unique N-terminal extension (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this composition, and Figure 1A shows the isoform structure.

claim: The N-terminal extension of NOCA-1d is not required for its function in the larval/adult epidermis.
source: The N-terminal extension was not required for function, since expression of an NHD::GFP fusion under the Pptrn-1 promoter was sufficient to rescue the double mutant phenotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on rescue data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The NHD of NOCA-1 is sufficient to function redundantly with PTRN-1 in the larval/adult epidermis to support organismal growth and development.
source: These results indicate that the NHD of NOCA-1 is sufficient to function redundantly with PTRN-1 in the larval/adult epidermis to support organismal growth and development.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the rescue experiments.

claim: The body epidermis is a large, thin multinucleated syncytial cell that covers the majority of the worm's body.
source: The body epidermis (gold in 3D view) is a large, thin multinucleated syncytial cell that covers the majority of the worm's body; rows of seam cells (pink) are embedded within the body epidermis in rows that run along either side of the worm.
evidence: The text explicitly describes this structure, and Figure 2B shows a schematic.

claim: Rows of seam cells are embedded within the body epidermis in rows that run along either side of the worm.
source: The body epidermis (gold in 3D view) is a large, thin multinucleated syncytial cell that covers the majority of the worm's body; rows of seam cells (pink) are embedded within the body epidermis in rows that run along either side of the worm.
evidence: The text explicitly describes this structure, and Figure 2B shows a schematic.

claim: The seam cells fuse to form syncytia at the mid-L4 stage.
source: The seam cells fuse to form syncytia at the mid-L4 stage (Chisholm and Hsiao, 2012; Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The text explicitly states this developmental event, citing a prior study and showing images in the figures.

claim: The epidermal microtubule array is composed of regularly spaced circumferential bundles.
source: As previously reported (Priess and Hirsh, 1986; Costa et al., 1997), the epidermal microtubule array is composed of regularly spaced circumferential bundles that appear as lines perpendicular to the larva/worm body axis in longitudinal sectional views (Figure 2B).
evidence: The text explicitly describes this structure, citing prior studies and showing images in Figure 2B.

claim: The density of microtubule bundles along the length of the worm is not significantly different from controls in the noca-1∆ mutant.
source: The density of microtubule bundles along the length of the worm was not significantly different from controls in the noca-1∆ mutant and was only slightly reduced in the ptrn-1∆ mutant (Figure 2C and Video 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure and video.

claim: The density of microtubule bundles along the length of the worm is only slightly reduced in the ptrn-1∆ mutant.
source: The density of microtubule bundles along the length of the worm was not significantly different from controls in the noca-1∆ mutant and was only slightly reduced in the ptrn-1∆ mutant (Figure 2C and Video 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure and video.

claim: Significantly fewer microtubule bundles are observed in the noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant.
source: In contrast, significantly fewer microtubule bundles were observed in the noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutant (Figure 2C and Video 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure and video.

claim: NOCA-1 and Patronin/PTRN-1 redundantly control the assembly of a circumferential microtubule array required for larval development.
source: We conclude that NOCA-1 and Patronin/PTRN-1 redundantly control the assembly of a circumferential microtubule array required for larval development.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the observed phenotypes.

claim: When only PTRN-1 is present (noca-1∆), microtubules appear less dynamic than in wild type.
source: When only PTRN-1 was present (noca-1∆), microtubules appeared less dynamic than in wild type, whereas microtubules exhibited apparently normal dynamics when only NOCA-1 was present (ptrn-1∆; Video 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on video analysis.

claim: When only NOCA-1 is present (ptrn-1∆), microtubules exhibit apparently normal dynamics.
source: When only PTRN-1 was present (noca-1∆), microtubules appeared less dynamic than in wild type, whereas microtubules exhibited apparently normal dynamics when only NOCA-1 was present (ptrn-1∆; Video 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on video analysis.

claim: The density of EB1 comets is substantially reduced when only PTRN-1 is present (noca-1∆).
source: Consistent with this impression, the density of EB1 comets was substantially reduced when only PTRN-1 was present (noca-1∆) but was comparable to controls when only NOCA-1 was present (ptrn-1∆; Figure 2D and Video 3).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure and video.

claim: The density of EB1 comets is comparable to controls when only NOCA-1 is present (ptrn-1∆).
source: Consistent with this impression, the density of EB1 comets was substantially reduced when only PTRN-1 was present (noca-1∆) but was comparable to controls when only NOCA-1 was present (ptrn-1∆; Figure 2D and Video 3).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure and video.

claim: The microtubule growth rate is reduced by approximately 20% compared to controls in worms expressing PTRN-1 only (noca-1∆).
source: The microtubule growth rate, measured by tracking of EB1 comets, was also reduced by ∼20% compared to controls in worms expressing PTRN-1 only (noca-1∆) but not in worm expressing NOCA-1 only (ptrn-1∆; Figure 2D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure.

claim: The microtubule growth rate is not reduced in worms expressing NOCA-1 only (ptrn-1∆).
source: The microtubule growth rate, measured by tracking of EB1 comets, was also reduced by ∼20% compared to controls in worms expressing PTRN-1 only (noca-1∆) but not in worm expressing NOCA-1 only (ptrn-1∆; Figure 2D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on data shown in the figure.

claim: The presence of NOCA-1 makes the microtubule arrays in the larval epidermis significantly more dynamic.
source: These results suggest that although either NOCA-1 or PTRN-1 can support the assembly of a circumferential microtubule array in the larval epidermis, the presence of NOCA-1 makes the arrays significantly more dynamic.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the dynamics measurements.

claim: In noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutants, seam cell syncytia are frequently branched/broken (71%).
source: In contrast, in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutants, seam cell syncytia were frequently branched/broken (71%; n = 17) as well as disconnected from the head epidermis (68%; n = 22; Figure 2E).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure.

claim: In noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutants, seam cell syncytia are frequently disconnected from the head epidermis (68%).
source: In contrast, in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ double mutants, seam cell syncytia were frequently branched/broken (71%; n = 17) as well as disconnected from the head epidermis (68%; n = 22; Figure 2E).
evidence: The text explicitly states this quantitative observation based on data shown in the figure.

claim: The cuticles of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutant worms become permeable to Hoechst dye, beginning approximately 24 hr after the L1 larval stage.
source: In addition to seam cell defects, the cuticles of noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutant worms became permeable to the normally excluded Hoechst dye, beginning ∼24 hr after the L1 larval stage (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on data shown in the figures.

claim: Defects in the epidermis and cuticle likely underlie the rupture phenotype with extrusion of internal tissues observed in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutant worms.
source: These defects in the epidermis and cuticle likely underlie the rupture phenotype with extrusion of internal tissues observed in noca-1∆; ptrn-1∆ mutant worms (Figure 1D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this inference based on the observed defects.

claim: NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 function in parallel to promote the assembly of a circumferential array of microtubule bundles that is required for the morphology and integrity of the larval/adult epidermis.
source: We conclude that NOCA-1 and PTRN-1 function in parallel to promote the assembly of a circumferential array of microtubule bundles that is required for the morphology and integrity of the larval/adult epidermis.
evidence: The text explicitly states this conclusion based on the cumulative results.

claim: NOCA-1 has a localization pattern very similar to that of γ-tubulin in the larval epidermis.
source: Imaging of a GFP fusion with NOCA-1 in the larval epidermis revealed that it had a localization pattern very similar to that of γ-tubulin; NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin were both observed in puncta in the epidermal syncytium where the microtubule bundles are present (Figure 3A, magnified insets) and also concentrated along the junctions between the epidermal body syncytium and the seam cells (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on imaging shown in the figures.

claim: NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin are both observed in puncta in the epidermal syncytium where the microtubule bundles are present.
source: Imaging of a GFP fusion with NOCA-1 in the larval epidermis revealed that it had a localization pattern very similar to that of γ-tubulin; NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin were both observed in puncta in the epidermal syncytium where the microtubule bundles are present (Figure 3A, magnified insets) and also concentrated along the junctions between the epidermal body syncytium and the seam cells (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on imaging shown in the figures.

claim: NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin are concentrated along the junctions between the epidermal body syncytium and the seam cells.
source: Imaging of a GFP fusion with NOCA-1 in the larval epidermis revealed that it had a localization pattern very similar to that of γ-tubulin; NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin were both observed in puncta in the epidermal syncytium where the microtubule bundles are present (Figure 3A, magnified insets) and also concentrated along the junctions between the epidermal body syncytium and the seam cells (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on imaging shown in the figures.

claim: The localization pattern of PTRN-1::GFP is distinct from that of NOCA-1 and γ-tubulin.
source: The localization pattern of PTRN-1::GFP was distinct.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation.

claim: PTRN-1::GFP is observed in stretches as well as puncta in the body syncytium.
source: Consistent with prior work (Jiang et al., 2014) PTRN-1::GFP was observed in stretches as well as puncta in the body syncytium.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation, citing prior work and showing images in Figure 3A.

claim: PTRN-1::GFP is observed in puncta within the seam cells but does not accumulate along the seam cell junctions.
source: PTRN-1::GFP was also observed in puncta within the seam cells but did not accumulate along the seam cell junctions.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation.

claim: Many puncta of both NOCA-1d::GFP and PTRN-1::GFP are observed coincident with the microtubule bundles in the body epidermis.
source: In double label images of NOCA-1d::GFP or PTRN-1::GFP with tagRFP::β-tubulin, many puncta of both proteins were observed coincident with the microtubule bundles in the body epidermis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on imaging shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The GIP-2::GFP signal in the larval epidermis is reduced by >80% compared to controls in epiDEG worms.
source: Quantification revealed that the GIP-2::GFP signal in the larval epidermis was reduced by >80% compared to controls in epiDEG worms whereas the signal in the germline was unaffected (Figure 3D), indicating the GFP-mediated degradation is efficient and tissue specific.

claim: The γ-tubulin complex functions together with NOCA-1 and in parallel to PTRN-1 for non-centrosomal microtubule array generation in the larval epidermis.

claim: noca-1 deletion results in an essentially identical phenotype to γ-tubulin depletion in the germline.
source: Imaging germline architecture in worms expressing a GFP-tagged plasma membrane probe along with mCherry-histone or GFP::β-tubulin revealed that noca-1 deletion resulted in an essentially identical phenotype to γ-tubulin depletion; in both cases, nuclei fell out of their compartments and formed clumps in the rachis center, indicating a dramatic failure in the function of the microtubule arrays in the compartments (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation based on imaging shown in the figures.

claim: In noca-1∆ and γ-tubulin-depleted germlines, nuclei fall out of their compartments and form clumps in the rachis center.
source: Imaging germline architecture in worms expressing a GFP-tagged plasma membrane probe along with mCherry-histone or GFP::β-tubulin revealed that noca-1 deletion resulted in an essentially identical phenotype to γ-tubulin depletion; in both cases, nuclei fell out of their compartments and formed clumps in the rachis center, indicating a dramatic failure in the function of the microtubule arrays in the compartments (Figure 4B,C).
